title: Topological robustness of thermally disordered lattices: From average structures to ensemble electronic properties
abstract: Band topology is usually assigned to a single crystal structure, yet at finite temperature a crystal is an ensemble of thermally disordered configurations with a fluctuating band gap. We ask whether the thermally averaged structure is a faithful proxy for this ensemble, taking Bi$_2$Se$_3$ as a representative topological insulator and classifying band ordering in each ab initio molecular dynamics snapshot by scaling the spin-orbit coupling. The averaged structure fails in two ways: it misses the Rashba-like spin splitting that instantaneous symmetry breaking produces in individual configurations, and it substantially underestimates the band-gap renormalization, whereas a small ensemble of harmonic Monte Carlo configurations reproduces both the mean and the spread of the gap. Using a band-inversion survival probability, we find that the band inversion of Bi$_2$Se$_3$ holds in every sampled configuration up to 600 K, above which individual configurations cross into normal band ordering well before the average gap closes. Topological robustness at finite temperature is thus a property of the distribution over configurations rather than of any single structure.
summary: This work examines how thermal disorder affects the topological properties of materials like $	ext{Bi}_2	ext{Se}_3$. The authors demonstrate that simply averaging the structure fails to capture crucial effects like instantaneous symmetry breaking. They conclude that true topological robustness at finite temperature depends on the statistical distribution of configurations, not the average structure itself.
main_problem: The study investigates whether the electronic properties, particularly band topology, of a material at finite temperature are accurately represented by averaging over the entire ensemble of thermally disordered configurations.
main_result: Topological robustness at finite temperature is a property of the entire distribution over configurations, not of any single instantaneous structure or the simple thermal average.
method: The authors employ ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations and compare the results from the time-averaged structure against ensembles generated by Monte Carlo sampling.
model_or_system: The physical system is $	ext{Bi}_2	ext{Se}_3$, a representative topological insulator. The model involves simulating the lattice structure under thermal disorder using DFT calculations.
key_observables: Band topology (band inversion), band gap renormalization, Rashba-like spin splitting, and band-inversion survival probability.
important_parameters: Temperature (up to 1050 K), Spin-Orbit Coupling (SOC) scaling parameter ($\lambda$), and the structural sampling method (AIMD vs. MCS).
main_assumptions: The primary assumption challenged is that the time-averaged structure ($\langle R angle$) is a faithful proxy for the ensemble average of electronic properties.
figures_summary: Figures compare band structures and lattice parameters derived from AIMD snapshots, Monte Carlo sampling, and the time-averaged structure, illustrating discrepancies in symmetry breaking and gap values.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem of finite-temperature averaging, applies DFT/AIMD to $	ext{Bi}_2	ext{Se}_3$, compares the results from the time-average versus the ensemble, and concludes that the distribution governs the topological stability.
why_interesting: The concept of topological robustness being governed by the statistical distribution of configurations rather than a single mean structure is highly relevant to understanding open quantum systems and materials under non-equilibrium or fluctuating conditions.
